#### Cinder Brand
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 60 feet
Cost: None
Release a streak of clinging ash.
Make a ranged Cultivation Attack.
Hit: Deal Fire, Necrotic, or Psychic damage and apply Ashen Brand.
| Cultivation Level | Damage |
| --- | --- |
| 1-4 | 1d8 |
| 5-10 | 2d8 |
| 11-16 | 3d8 |
| 17-20 | 4d8 |
Once per turn when Cinder Brand hits, choose one:
reduce healing received by your Proficiency Bonus until the start of your next turn;
create one Remnant in an unoccupied space adjacent to the target;
move one Remnant within 30 feet up to 10 feet;
suppress one ordinary source of Temporary HP already affecting the target until the start of your next turn.

### Darkness
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 120 feet
Area: 15-foot-radius sphere
Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute
Cost: None
Create a sphere of supernatural Darkness centered anywhere within range.
The darkness radiates from a central point, spreads around corners, and cannot extend through walls.
A creature with Darkvision can see through this Darkness. Nonmagical light cannot illuminate it.
#### Contesting Light
If a Light-sphere effect is created inside your Darkness, the creator of the Light effect makes a Cultivation Check against your Cultivation Save DC.
Successful Check: Your Darkness is countered and the Light effect functions normally.Failed Check: The Light effect functions only as an ordinary light source and cannot illuminate your Darkness.
#### Persistent Darkness
Augment - 2 CP: Your Darkness persists for its remaining duration without Concentration.
You may apply this augment after creating the Darkness on your turn without spending an action.

add your Proficiency Bonus to the damage if the target is Kindled.

Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 90 feet
Cost: 0 CP
Target: One creature or object you can target
Release a distant ray, comet fragment, constellation needle, pale astral bolt, star-metal spark, or cold point of starlight.
Make a ranged Cultivation Attack roll. On a hit, choose Radiant, Force, or Cold damage and deal:
CL 1-4: 1d8 damage;
CL 5-10: 2d8 damage;
CL 11-16: 3d8 damage;
CL 17-20: 4d8 damage.
Once per turn when Starbolt hits, you may apply Stellar Mark to the target until the start of your next turn.
Aligned Benefit: If you are Aligned, Starbolt’s range increases by 30 feet.

source_rows.effect:
### Cast Axe
Action Type: Action
Canonical Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Timing Detail: Special Attack
Factory Routing: combat_action_row; preserve attack-replacement detail
Parent Action: Attack
Replaces Attacks: 1
Range: Weapon thrown range, or 20/60 feet for a handaxe-like thrown axe
Target: One creature or object
Cost: None
Requirement: You must throw an axe weapon with the thrown property or a GM-approved throwing axe.
Make a thrown weapon attack with the axe. On a hit, the attack deals normal weapon damage. Then choose one Cast rider.
**Shock Cast.** The target cannot take Reactions against you until the start of your next turn.
**Lodging Cast.** The axe lodges and the target gains Bite from you until the start of your next turn. A creature can remove the lodged axe as an Object Interaction if it has a free hand and is not Incapacitated.
**Turning Cast.** If the target is no more than one size larger than you, it must choose either to be pushed 5 feet or to have its Speed reduced by 5 feet until the start of your next turn.
**Splinter Cast.** If the target is an unattended object, wooden barrier, fragile cover, shield, banner pole, rope, vine, or similar object, add your Proficiency Bonus to the damage.
If you throw your only axe, you are no longer wielding it until you retrieve it, draw another weapon, or a talent returns it.

Action Type: Action
Canonical Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Timing Detail: Special Attack
Factory Routing: combat_action_row; preserve attack-replacement detail

Replaces Attacks: 1

**Hamper.** The target's Speed is reduced by 5 feet until the start of your next turn.
You may choose only one rider unless a talent says otherwise.

source_rows.effect:
### Base Ability: Anchor the Link
Action Type: Reaction
Factory Combat Bucket: reaction
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 30 feet
Trigger: You, an ally, a creature bearing one of your Tethers, or an object linked by your Chains would be pushed, pulled, knocked Prone, moved involuntarily, dropped, or carried into a hazard
Cost: 1 CP
You fasten a chain to a stable surface, heavy object, your own body, the ground, a wall, a formation anchor, or a spiritual point of resistance.
Choose one:
reduce forced movement by 10 feet;
grant Advantage on the triggering saving throw against forced movement or Prone;
prevent a fall if a stable anchor exists within 30 feet;
allow the target to hang safely until the start of its next turn;
prevent the target from entering a hazard if reducing the movement is enough to keep it clear.
At Core Formation Realm, reduce forced movement by 20 feet instead of 10 feet.
Anchor the Link is the defensive and containment ability of Chains. Most rescue, anti-teleport, battlefield-control, and prison talents modify this ability.

### Base Ability: Chain Lash
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 30 feet
Target: One creature or object
Cost: None
You strike with a physical chain, manifested link, hooked cord, shackle-ribbon, seal-chain, ghostly restraint, or similar expression.
Make a melee or ranged Cultivation Attack roll.
On a hit, the target takes Bludgeoning or Slashing damage based on your Realm:
Mortal: 1d8
Foundation: 2d8
Core Formation: 3d8
Nascent Soul: 4d8
Once per turn when Chain Lash hits, choose one minor link effect:
pull the target 5 feet toward you;
push the target 5 feet away from you;
reduce the target’s Speed by 5 feet until the start of your next turn;
gain Advantage on the next check you make to Grapple the target before the start of your next turn;
attach a harmless visible Link to the target until the start of your next turn.
Chain Lash is the default attack expression of the sphere. Most offensive Chains talents modify Chain Lash, trigger after Chain Lash hits, or replace the minor link effect.

### Base Ability: Set the Tether
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 30 feet
Target: One creature, object, surface, or point you can see
Duration: Until the start of your next turn
Cost: 1 CP
You throw, manifest, write, or fasten a chain that connects the target to you, to a stable surface, or to another point you can see within range.
If the target is an unwilling creature, it makes a Strength saving throw.
Failed Save: The target becomes Bound until the start of your next turn. The Tether has a maximum length of 30 feet.
Successful Save: The target’s Speed is reduced by 5 feet until the start of your next turn.
If you target a willing creature or unattended object, no saving throw is required.
You may use Set the Tether to pull an unattended object weighing no more than 25 pounds x your CL up to 20 feet toward you.
Set the Tether is the main binding and positioning ability. Most restraint, pulling, prison, and link talents modify this ability.

### Base Sphere Abilities
When you learn Daemonic Cultivation, gain Demon Seed, Devour Essence, and Daemonic Augment.
#### Demon Seed
Classification: Forbidden Daemonic Root
Action Type: Bonus Action
Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Duration: 1 minute
Cost: 1 CP or 1 Stamina
Plant or awaken a Demon Seed in your body, dantian, meridians, or soul. The Seed is a forbidden method-root, not a Demon Core. It does not make you a demon; it opens the second furnace through which the daemonic scripture can breathe.
While Demon Seed is active:
your Daemonic talents may be used;
you gain Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your Daemonic key ability modifier;
once per turn when you hit with a weapon attack, Unarmed Strike, or Cultivation Attack, add 1d4 Necrotic, Psychic, or Force damage;
you have Advantage on saving throws against Frightened;
you have Disadvantage on checks made to appear spiritually pure unless you suppress all visible signs.
At CL 5, the extra damage becomes 1d6.
At CL 11, the extra damage becomes 1d8.
At CL 17, the extra damage becomes 1d10.
When Demon Seed ends, if you used Overdraw during its duration, make a Wisdom saving throw against your Daemonic Save DC. On a failure, gain 1 additional Corruption.
#### Devour Essence
Classification: Forbidden Daemonic Technique
Action Type: Multi-Mode
Canonical Action Type: Multi-Mode
Factory Combat Bucket: split_required
Split Candidate Buckets: bonus_action, reaction
Timing Detail: Bonus Action or Reaction
Factory Routing: split_modes_before_character_action_programming
Split Review Decision: split_required_distinct_combat_buckets
Recommended Factory Realization: modes=BONUS_ACTION_DEVOUR->bonus_action, REACTION_DEVOUR->reaction
Range: 30 feet
Cost: None
Use Devour Essence when one of the following happens within range:
a hostile creature is reduced to 0 HP;
a creature fails a saving throw against one of your Daemonic talents;
you score a Critical Hit;
a creature bearing your demonic mark takes damage;
an ongoing summoned, possessed, spirit, fiendish, undead, or demonic effect ends.
Gain 1 Devoured Essence.
You can use Devour Essence once per round.
If the triggering creature is at least your Realm or has a CR/level equal to at least half your CL, you may instead gain 2 Devoured Essence, but you also gain 1 Corruption.
#### Daemonic Augment
Classification: Forbidden Amplification
Action Type: Special Trigger
Canonical Action Type: Special Trigger
Factory Combat Bucket: passive
Timing Detail: No Action, once per turn
Factory Routing: triggered_passive_modifier_row
Cost: 1 CP, 1 Stamina, or 1 Devoured Essence
Trigger: You use a sphere talent, weapon attack, Unarmed Strike, or Cultivation Attack that deals damage, imposes a condition, moves a creature, creates a zone, or forces a saving throw.
Twist the technique with daemonic hunger. Choose one:
add Proficiency Bonus to one damage roll;
impose Disadvantage on one Concentration saving throw caused by the triggering effect;
if the triggering effect moves a creature, increase the movement by 5 feet;
if the triggering effect creates Difficult Terrain, one creature that fails a save also cannot take Reactions until the start of your next turn;
if the triggering effect deals Necrotic, Psychic, Fire, Poison, Acid, Force, or weapon damage, ignore ordinary Resistance to one of those damage types for that instance;
mark one damaged creature until the start of your next turn. The first time you damage the marked creature before the mark ends, gain 1 Devoured Essence.
Daemonic Augment may modify non-Daemonic sphere talents, but only once per turn. This is one of the main reasons the sphere is forbidden.

#### Daemonic Augment
Classification: Forbidden Amplification
Action Type: Special Trigger
Canonical Action Type: Special Trigger
Factory Combat Bucket: passive
Timing Detail: No Action, once per turn
Factory Routing: triggered_passive_modifier_row
Cost: 1 CP, 1 Stamina, or 1 Devoured Essence
Trigger: You use a sphere talent, weapon attack, Unarmed Strike, or Cultivation Attack that deals damage, imposes a condition, moves a creature, creates a zone, or forces a saving throw.
Twist the technique with daemonic hunger. Choose one:
add Proficiency Bonus to one damage roll;
impose Disadvantage on one Concentration saving throw caused by the triggering effect;
if the triggering effect moves a creature, increase the movement by 5 feet;
if the triggering effect creates Difficult Terrain, one creature that fails a save also cannot take Reactions until the start of your next turn;
if the triggering effect deals Necrotic, Psychic, Fire, Poison, Acid, Force, or weapon damage, ignore ordinary Resistance to one of those damage types for that instance;
mark one damaged creature until the start of your next turn. The first time you damage the marked creature before the mark ends, gain 1 Devoured Essence.
Daemonic Augment may modify non-Daemonic sphere talents, but only once per turn. This is one of the main reasons the sphere is forbidden.

#### Devour Essence
Classification: Forbidden Daemonic Technique
Action Type: Multi-Mode
Canonical Action Type: Multi-Mode
Factory Combat Bucket: split_required
Split Candidate Buckets: bonus_action, reaction
Timing Detail: Bonus Action or Reaction
Factory Routing: split_modes_before_character_action_programming
Split Review Decision: split_required_distinct_combat_buckets
Recommended Factory Realization: modes=BONUS_ACTION_DEVOUR->bonus_action, REACTION_DEVOUR->reaction
Range: 30 feet
Cost: None
Use Devour Essence when one of the following happens within range:
a hostile creature is reduced to 0 HP;
a creature fails a saving throw against one of your Daemonic talents;
you score a Critical Hit;
a creature bearing your demonic mark takes damage;
an ongoing summoned, possessed, spirit, fiendish, undead, or demonic effect ends.
Gain 1 Devoured Essence.
You can use Devour Essence once per round.
If the triggering creature is at least your Realm or has a CR/level equal to at least half your CL, you may instead gain 2 Devoured Essence, but you also gain 1 Corruption.

source_rows.effect:
### Darkness
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 120 feet
Area: 15-foot-radius sphere
Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute
Cost: None
Create a sphere of supernatural Darkness centered anywhere within range.
The darkness radiates from a central point, spreads around corners, and cannot extend through walls.
A creature with Darkvision can see through this Darkness. Nonmagical light cannot illuminate it.
#### Contesting Light
If a Light-sphere effect is created inside your Darkness, the creator of the Light effect makes a Cultivation Check against your Cultivation Save DC.
Successful Check: Your Darkness is countered and the Light effect functions normally.Failed Check: The Light effect functions only as an ordinary light source and cannot illuminate your Darkness.
#### Persistent Darkness
Augment - 2 CP: Your Darkness persists for its remaining duration without Concentration.
You may apply this augment after creating the Darkness on your turn without spending an action.

### Meld
Action Type: Ritual Procedure
Canonical Action Type: Ritual Procedure
Factory Routing: procedure_ledger_not_combat_action
Timing Detail: 10 minutes
Range: Touch
Target: One creature
Duration: Concentration, up to 1 hour
Cost: None
Grant the target one Meld talent you know.
An unwilling creature may make a Wisdom saving throw to resist receiving the Meld.
A creature may benefit from only one Meld talent granted by the same cultivator unless another ability explicitly says otherwise.
#### Rapid Meld
Augment - 1 CP: Reduce the activation time to 1 Action.
#### Persistent Meld
Augment - 2 CP: The Meld persists for its remaining duration without Concentration.
You may apply this augment after granting the Meld on your turn without spending an action.

source_rows.effect:
#### Rouse Lesser Dead
Action Type: Ritual Procedure
Canonical Action Type: Ritual Procedure
Factory Routing: procedure_ledger_not_combat_action
Timing Detail: Ritual
Time: 10 minutes
Range: Touch
Target: One Common corpse or suitable set of remains
Duration: 8 hours, or until the servant is destroyed or dismissed
Cost: 1 CP
Control Load: 1
Requirement: You must have enough unused Death Control Limit to maintain the servant, and the target must be a legal corpse under the Corpse Availability rules.
You animate the target with grave Qi as one Lesser Corpse Servant. It appears in the corpse's space with full Hit Points and uses the Lesser Corpse Servant stat block below.
The servant is one undead asset. It counts against your Death Control Limit, acts immediately after your turn, and is commanded according to Commanding Death Servants. If it is not commanded, it takes the Dodge action and moves only as permitted by those rules.
A Lesser Corpse Servant does not contain the original soul unless another talent says so. It can follow simple commands, perform labor, carry objects, open doors, keep watch, pull carts, dig, clean, guard a threshold, or fight if commanded.
You may maintain only one Lesser Corpse Servant created by this base ability at a time. You may dismiss that servant without taking an action on your turn. If you complete this ritual while one of your Lesser Corpse Servants from this ability still exists, the earlier servant must be dismissed before the new one is created.
If the corpse is protected, sacred, claimed, preserved, or socially taboo, animating it may be impossible without a rite, permission, or a successful opposed Cultivation Check.

source_rows.effect:
#### Withering Hand
Action Type: Multi-Mode
Canonical Action Type: Multi-Mode
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Timing Detail: Special Attack or Action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row_with_attack_replacement_mode
Split Review Decision: same_bucket_attack_replacement_mode
Recommended Factory Realization: modes=MELEE_ATTACK_REPLACEMENT->action, RANGED_ACTION->action
Range: Melee reach or 60 feet
Target: One creature
Cost: None
You strike with grave Qi, either through a touch, weapon, talisman, funerary seal, or bolt of pale force.
When you take the Attack action, you may replace one attack with Withering Hand, making a Cultivation Attack roll against one creature within melee reach. Alternatively, you may use an Action to make a ranged Cultivation Attack roll against one creature within 60 feet.
Hit: The target takes Necrotic damage based on your CL.
CL 1-4: 1d8 Necrotic damage.
CL 5-10: 2d8 Necrotic damage.
CL 11-16: 3d8 Necrotic damage.
CL 17-20: 4d8 Necrotic damage.
Once per turn when you hit a creature with Withering Hand, healing the target receives is reduced by your Proficiency Bonus until the start of your next turn.
This healing reduction applies once to each healing event. It does not reduce healing below 0.

#### Destructive Blast
Base Sphere Ability
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 30 feet
Target: One creature or object
Duration: Instantaneous
Cost: 0 CP
You release cultivated destruction against one creature or object within range.
Choose one Blast Type talent you possess. You may also apply no more than one Blast Shape talent you possess.
If you do not apply a Blast Shape talent, release an unshaped blast:
make one ranged Cultivation Attack against one creature or object within range;
on a hit, the target takes your Destructive Blast damage and suffers any applicable effects of the selected Blast Type.
If you know no other Blast Type, you use Unadorned Ruin.

### Broken-Rhythm Strike
Action Type: Action
Canonical Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Timing Detail: Special Attack
Factory Routing: combat_action_row; preserve attack-replacement detail
Range: Weapon reach or unarmed reach
Cost: None
Replace one attack when you take the Attack action.
Make an Unarmed Strike using the Damage option, an improvised melee weapon attack, or a melee weapon attack.
Hit: The attack deals normal damage, and the target becomes Off-Rhythm from you until the start of your next turn.
Miss by 5 or Less: You may choose to create a False Opening for the target. If you do, the target becomes Off-Rhythm from you immediately after it next attacks you before the start of your next turn.
Miss by More than 5: No effect.

source_rows.effect:
### Reeling Step
Action Type: Bonus Action
Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: Self
Cost: None
You move up to 10 feet in a loose, swaying, indirect, or foolish-looking path.
This movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks from one creature you can see.
Before or after this movement, choose one creature within 10 feet that can see you. That creature must make a Wisdom saving throw against your Drunken Style Save DC.
Failed Save: The creature becomes Off-Rhythm from you until the start of your next turn.
Successful Save: The creature is not Off-Rhythm, but it cannot make Opportunity Attacks against you during the movement granted by this Reeling Step.
You cannot use Reeling Step if your Speed is 0.

source_rows.effect:
### Swaying Guard
Action Type: Reaction
Factory Combat Bucket: reaction
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Trigger: A creature you can see makes an attack roll against you
Cost: None
You loosen your body, slip the line, lean late, or let the strike pass through the place you appeared to occupy.
Use Swaying Guard in one of the following ways:
If the attacker is Off-Rhythm from you, impose Disadvantage on the triggering attack roll.
If you moved at least 5 feet since the end of your last turn, add your Proficiency Bonus to your AC against the triggering attack.
You choose after seeing the attack roll but before knowing whether the attack hits or misses.
If the triggering attack misses, you may move 5 feet. This movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks from the triggering attacker.
You may expend Martial Focus to use Swaying Guard without spending your Reaction. Once you do so, you cannot use Swaying Guard again until the start of your next turn.

#### Sense the Ledger
Action Type: Multi-Mode
Canonical Action Type: Multi-Mode
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_plus_exploration_procedure
Split Review Decision: single_combat_action_plus_procedure_variant
Recommended Factory Realization: action_id=ACT_FATE_SENSE_THE_LEDGER_STUDY_ACTION->action; procedures=ONE_MINUTE_OBSERVATION
Timing Detail: Study action in encounter time, or 1 minute of observation in exploration time
Range: 30 feet
Cost: None
You read the local pressure of fate.
Choose one creature, object, oath, doorway, battlefield feature, game of chance, written name, or visible ritual within range. Make a Wisdom or Charisma Cultivation Check against a DC set by the GM.
Success: Learn one of the following, if present:
whether the target is affected by a Fate talent;
whether the target carries supernatural luck or misfortune;
whether a game of chance, drawing of lots, wager, or random selection is being supernaturally manipulated;
whether a visible oath, name, seal, contract, or red-thread bond is fate-active;
whether the place is auspicious, ominous, or strongly connected to a destined meeting or calamity;
whether a creature has recently altered fate within the scene.
Sense the Ledger does not reveal exact mechanics, full stat blocks, private thoughts, future events, or hidden locations automatically.
At CL 10, the range becomes 60 feet.

#### Twist of Fate
Action Type: Reaction
Factory Combat Bucket: reaction
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Trigger: A creature within 30 feet that you can perceive makes an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw
Cost: 1 CP
Use Limit: Once per round
After the d20 is rolled but before the outcome is known, choose one:
add your Fate Die to the roll;
subtract your Fate Die from the roll.
You must be able to perceive the creature or the immediate consequences of the roll.
Twist of Fate cannot affect a roll already modified by another Fate talent from you.
At CL 10, the range becomes 60 feet.

A Feint does not require a weapon unless a talent explicitly says otherwise.

#### Cultivate Blossom
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 60 feet
Target: One creature, object, or unoccupied 5-foot space
Duration: 1 hour or until bloomed
Cost: None
Create one dormant spiritual Blossom.

The Blossom is applied automatically.

Make a ranged Cultivation Attack.
Hit: Apply the Blossom.
Miss: No effect.
##### Immediate Bloom
When you create a Blossom, you may cause it to bloom immediately as part of the same Action.
##### Delayed Bloom
As a Bonus Action, cause one of your dormant Blossoms within 60 feet to bloom.
Choose one Blossom talent you know and pay its CP cost.

#### Flowing Response
Action Type: Reaction
Factory Combat Bucket: reaction
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Trigger: When a creature you can see makes a melee attack roll against you; when a creature within your reach attempts to Grapple or Shove you; or when a creature within your reach forces you to make a Strength or Dexterity saving throw to avoid being moved, knocked Prone, Grappled, or Restrained.
Cost: None
Use Limit: Once per round
You receive an incoming force and decide where it continues.
You may use Flowing Response when one of the following triggers occurs:
a creature you can see makes a melee attack roll against you;
a creature within your reach attempts to Grapple or Shove you;
a creature within your reach forces you to make a Strength or Dexterity saving throw to avoid being moved, knocked Prone, Grappled, or Restrained.
Choose the matching response.
##### Yield Against an Attack
Increase your AC against the triggering melee attack by your Proficiency Bonus.
If the attack misses, the response succeeds. After the attack resolves, you may move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks from the triggering creature, then apply one Response talent you know.
##### Yield Against Control
Gain Advantage on the triggering saving throw against the Grapple, Shove, forced movement, Prone effect, or Restrained effect.
If you succeed on the saving throw, the response succeeds. After the effect resolves, you may move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks from the triggering creature, then apply one Response talent you know.

source_rows.effect:
### Counterpressure
Action Type: Reaction
Factory Combat Bucket: reaction
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Trigger: You, a creature, or an object within 5 feet of yourself or one Pressure Anchor you can perceive within 60 feet takes damage, would be pushed or pulled, or would be knocked Prone
Cost: 1 CP
Release opposing pressure.
Choose one:
#### Cushion the Blow
Reduce the triggering damage.
| Cultivation Level | Damage Reduction |
| --- | --- |
| 1-10 | 1d8 + Path key ability modifier |
| 11-16 | 2d8 + Path key ability modifier |
| 17-20 | 3d8 + Path key ability modifier |
#### Refuse the Movement
Reduce the triggering forced movement by the listed distance.
| Cultivation Level | Forced-Movement Reduction |
| --- | --- |
| 1-4 | 10 feet |
| 5-10 | 15 feet |
| 11-16 | 20 feet |

source_rows.effect:
### Base Technique - External Weight Shift
Tag: Field Art.
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 60 feet.
Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute.
Cost: 1 CP or Stamina.
Choose one creature or object no larger than Large. If the target is willing, you may choose Body Lightening or Body Heavying for it. If the target is unwilling, choose Burden or Uplift.
Burden: The target makes a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, its Speed is reduced by 10 feet, its jump distance is halved, and it has Disadvantage on Strength (Athletics) and Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks. At the end of each of its turns, it repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. On a successful initial save, its Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of its next turn.
Uplift: The target makes a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, its first movement on its next turn is unstable: it must spend 10 feet of movement to remain grounded, or it rises 10 feet upward and then falls at the end of the turn if nothing holds it aloft. On a successful save, it rises only 5 feet or may immediately fall Prone to avoid the rise.
Objects: The GM determines how increased or decreased weight affects doors, bridges, ropes, carts, armor, siege engines, or carried objects. Gravity does not automatically destroy objects without a talent that deals damage or causes structural stress.

source_rows.effect:
### Base Ability - Weight Shift
Action Type: Bonus Action
Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: Self.
Duration: Until the start of your next turn.
Cost: 0 for the basic self version.
Choose one mode: Body Lightening, Body Heavying, or Neutral Weight.
You may change modes only once on each of your turns unless a talent says otherwise. If you are Incapacitated, your Weight Shift becomes Neutral Weight.
#### Body Lightening
Until the start of your next turn, your body becomes lighter, quicker, and less bound to the ground.
Benefits:
Your Speed increases by 10 feet.
Your jump distance increases by a number of feet equal to 5 + your Proficiency Bonus.
You reduce any falling damage you take by an amount equal to 5 times your Proficiency Bonus.
You gain Advantage on Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks made to escape a Grapple or move across narrow, fragile, or unstable footing.
If you move at least 10 feet before making a melee attack on your turn, you may use your Gravity key ability in place of Strength or Dexterity for that attack roll if the weapon is an unarmed strike, simple melee weapon, monk-like martial implement, spear, sword, staff, or other GM-approved mobile martial weapon.
Body Lightening does not grant flight by itself.
#### Body Heavying
Until the start of your next turn, your body becomes denser, more rooted, and harder to displace.
Benefits:
Your Speed is reduced by 5 feet, to a minimum of 5 feet.
You count as one size larger when resisting Shove, Grapple, forced movement, and effects that would knock you Prone.
You gain Advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws made to resist forced movement or being knocked Prone.
Your carrying, dragging, lifting, and pushing capacity doubles.
If you do not move more than half your Speed on your turn, the first melee weapon attack or Unarmed Strike you hit with before the start of your next turn deals additional damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. The damage type is the attack’s normal damage type, or Force if the attack is a supernatural Gravity technique.
Body Heavying does not increase your size and does not automatically increase weapon reach.
#### Neutral Weight
You return to normal weight. Ending Weight Shift early requires no action on your turn.

Action Type: Action

Range: 60 feet
Target: One creature or object

source_rows.effect:
#### Create Figment
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 60 feet
Area: One 10-foot cube
Duration: Concentration, up to 10 minutes
Cost: None
Tags: Image, Figment, Premise
You create the image or sound of something that is not actually there. Examples include a wall, beast, cultivator, banner, footstep, voice, warning bell, spirit-lantern, falling stone, corpse, door, or patch of false terrain.
The figment’s maximum area increases with your Cultivation Level.
| CL | Maximum Figment Size |
| --- | --- |
| 1-4 | 10-foot cube |
| 5-10 | 15-foot cube |
| 11-16 | 20-foot cube |
| 17-20 | 25-foot cube |
As long as you are within range of the figment, you may use your Action to move it to another point within range. As it moves, you may alter its appearance so the movement seems natural, such as making a false beast run or a false guard gesture. If you do not use your Action to control it, the figment repeats a simple motion or remains still.
When a creature that can perceive the figment makes an attack roll, targets a creature with a harmful effect, moves willingly, takes a Reaction, or makes a Perception, Insight, Investigation, or Survival check while acting on the figment as if it were real, you may force that creature to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the creature gains one False Premise from you until the start of your next turn.
Augment 1 CP: The figment includes both sight and sound. If you have Sensory talents, you may apply any of those sensory layers as part of the same figment.
Augment 1 CP: Increase the figment’s maximum area by one step: 20-foot cube at CL 1-4, 30-foot cube at CL 5-10, 40-foot cube at CL 11-16, and 50-foot cube at CL 17-20.
Augment 2 CP: The figment lasts for its remaining duration without Concentration. You may apply this augment on your turn after creating the figment without using an Action.

source_rows.effect:
### First Circuit Method
Action Type: Passive
Canonical Action Type: Passive
Factory Combat Bucket: passive
Timing Detail: Passive / Charge Rider
Factory Routing: passive_or_modifier_row
Range: Self
Cost: None
When you first gain the Lightning sphere, your meridians learn to hold a brief seed of unstable potential. This is called a First Circuit.
A First Circuit is not a full Charge and does not make you vulnerable to hostile Lightning talents unless a feature specifically says so. It is the internal spark that lets Lightning cultivation move through the body before it escapes into the world.
Once on each of your turns, when you use Gather Charge on yourself, a held weapon, a worn item, or a Lightning focus you are touching, choose one Circuit expression. The chosen expression lasts until the Charge ends.
**Body Circuit.** Before the Charge ends, when you deal lightning damage or consume a Charge, you may move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks from one creature damaged by your Lightning sphere this turn.
**Edge Circuit.** Before the Charge ends, the next time you hit with an unarmed strike, weapon attack, Lightning Lash, or Lightning talent delivered through a held implement, you deal additional lightning damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
**Nerve Circuit.** Before the Charge ends, when you would have your Speed reduced, be knocked Prone, or be denied Reactions by a non-Secret effect, you may discharge the Circuit to gain Advantage on the saving throw against that effect. If no saving throw is allowed, reduce the penalty by one step: ignore a Speed reduction of 10 feet or less, stand from Prone by spending 5 fewer feet of movement, or regain your Reaction at the start of your next turn.
**Conduction Circuit.** Before the Charge ends, when you apply Charge to a creature, object, formation node, talisman, weapon, armor, or 5-foot space, you may make yourself Conductive until the start of your next turn. While Conductive this way, your next Lightning talent that requires a Conductive Path may treat yourself, your held weapon, or your worn armor as the starting point of that path.
You may discharge only one First Circuit per round.

source_rows.effect:
### Gather Charge
Action Type: Bonus Action
Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 30 feet
Target: Yourself, one object you can see, one weapon you are holding, one willing creature you can see, one formation node you can see, or one unoccupied 5-foot space you can see
Cost: None
Duration: Until the start of your next turn
You gather unstable Lightning Qi and place a Charge on the target.
If you Charge a weapon you are holding, the next time you hit with that weapon before the Charge ends, you may consume the Charge to deal additional lightning damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
If you Charge yourself, you gain Advantage on the next Dexterity saving throw you make before the Charge ends against lightning, thunder, paralysis, forced movement, or being knocked Prone.
If you Charge a 5-foot space, the space becomes Conductive. The first time a creature enters that space before the Charge ends, you may end the Charge to deal lightning damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus to that creature. A creature can take this damage only once per turn.
At Foundation Realm, the range becomes 60 feet. At Core Formation, you may create two Charges with one use of Gather Charge, provided they are within range and do not exceed your Charge limit.

source_rows.effect:
### Lightning Lash
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 60 feet
Target: One creature or unattended object you can see
Cost: None
Make a ranged Cultivation Attack.
Hit: The target takes lightning damage equal to 1d8 + your Lightning key ability modifier.
The damage increases by 1d8 at CL 5, CL 11, and CL 17.
When Lightning Lash hits, choose one basic rider:
Charge: The target gains a Charge until the start of your next turn.
Jolt: The target cannot take Reactions against you until the start of your next turn.
Flash: Sparks reveal the target’s outline. Until the start of your next turn, the target cannot benefit from being unseen against you unless it has Total Cover or a stronger concealment effect.
Arc: If another creature or object within 5 feet of the target is Conductive or Charged, it takes lightning damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. This Arc cannot trigger additional Arcs unless a talent says otherwise.
Lightning Lash is a Cultivation Attack, not a weapon attack, unless a talent says otherwise.

source_rows.effect:
#### Magma Glob
Classification: Magma Base Attack
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 60 feet
Cost: None
Launch molten stone, slag, obsidian shards, or volcanic force at one creature or object.
Make a ranged Cultivation Attack.
Hit: The target takes Fire or Bludgeoning damage, chosen when you attack.
Damage by Cultivation Level:
• CL 1-4: 1d10
• CL 5-10: 2d10
• CL 11-16: 3d10
• CL 17-20: 4d10
Once per turn when Magma Glob hits, choose one:
• create one 5-foot patch of Molten Terrain adjacent to the target until the start of your next turn;
• apply Heat Pressure until the start of your next turn;
• push the target 5 feet if it is Large or smaller;
• create one 5-foot patch of Obsidian Terrain adjacent to the target for 1 minute.
Magma Glob is powerful for a base elemental attack because Magma is restricted. It is still not a siege technique by itself.

#### Laughing Staff and Borrowed Weapon - Base Weapon Tool
You are proficient with quarterstaffs, staffs, and improvised weapons used through Monkey Style.
Your Monkey Style improvised weapons deal 1d6 damage unless their normal damage would be higher.
Examples include stools, bottles, bricks, cooking pots, chains, loose stones, ladders, teapots, fruit, shoes, roof tiles, sleeves weighted with coins, and stolen weapons used incorrectly.
While Capering Footwork is active, hitting with a staff, Unarmed Strike, or improvised weapon may spend your Monkey Link on a base Finish.
Your Monkey Style improvised weapons count as magical while you wield them when a rule distinguishes magical and nonmagical attacks.

source_rows.effect:
##### Qi Bond
Classification: Base Qiweaving Ability
Action Type: Bonus Action
Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 30 feet
Target: One creature, object, or Active Qi Pattern
Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute
Cost: None
Attempt to form a thread between your circulation and the target’s Qi pattern.
A willing creature, an unattended object, or an Active Qi Pattern you created is bonded automatically.
Against an unwilling creature, attended object, or hostile Active Qi Pattern, make a ranged Cultivation Attack. If the target is an Active Qi Pattern, treat its AC as equal to its creator’s Cultivation Save DC. If the creator is unknown, use 10 + Pattern Rank.
Hit: Create a Qi Bond.
Miss: No bond forms.
While the bond lasts, you may use your Action on each of your turns to apply one Bond talent you know to the target.
Unless a Bond talent says otherwise, the Qi Bond ends if:
the target is ever outside your Qi Bond range;
the target has Total Cover from you;
you use your Action for anything other than applying or maintaining a Bond talent;
you lose Concentration.
###### Persistent Qi Bond
Augment - 2 CP: The Qi Bond persists for its remaining duration without Concentration.
You may apply this augment after creating the bond on your turn without spending an Action.

##### Turbulent Field
Classification: Base Qiweaving Ability
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: Self
Area: 5-foot-radius Emanation
Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute
Cost: None
You emit a field of unstable Qi.
If the campaign uses wild magic or Qi-deviation rules, increase the instability chance of creatures inside the area by 50 percent.
If the campaign does not use a separate instability system, use the following fallback.
The first time on a turn that a creature inside the area activates a technique that costs CP or casts a spell using a spell slot, it makes a Constitution saving throw.
Failed Save: The technique is Turbulent until it resolves. A Turbulent technique suffers one complication chosen by the GM or rolled from a campaign-appropriate table, such as visible backlash, noisy activation, reduced range, accidental self-exposure, or minor damage to an unattended nearby object.
The fallback complication should be inconvenient but should not normally waste the technique unless another Turbulence talent says so.
The area radius increases by Realm:
Cultivation Level: 1-4 - Radius: 5 feet
Cultivation Level: 5-10 - Radius: 10 feet
Cultivation Level: 11-16 - Radius: 15 feet
Cultivation Level: 17-20 - Radius: 20 feet
###### Lingering Turbulence
Augment - 2 CP: The Turbulent Field persists for its remaining duration without Concentration.
You may apply this augment after creating the field on your turn without spending an Action.

##### Unweave Pattern
Classification: Base Qiweaving Ability
Action Type: Ritual Procedure
Canonical Action Type: Ritual Procedure
Factory Routing: procedure_ledger_not_combat_action
Timing Detail: 10 minutes
Range: 30 feet
Target: One creature, object, location, or Active Qi Pattern
Duration: Instantaneous
Cost: None
Attempt to end one Active Qi Pattern on the target.
If the pattern’s Pattern Rank is equal to or lower than half your Proficiency Bonus, rounded down, it ends automatically.
Otherwise, make a Qiweaving Check against the pattern.
Successful Check: The pattern ends.
Failed Check: The pattern remains.
Unweave Pattern cannot end a Domain, Secret Inheritance, Formation project, artifact-level effect, or campaign-scale working unless a talent, project, or GM ruling explicitly permits it.
###### Rapid Unweave
Augment - 1 CP: Reduce the Action Type to Action.
If you Ready this Action to disrupt a technique as it is activated, resolve Unweave Pattern when the triggering technique is being created. On a successful check, the technique fails and any Action, CP, spell slot, or limited use spent on it is lost.
###### Broad Unweave
Augment - 1 CP: Attempt to unweave a number of additional Active Qi Patterns on the same target equal to half your Proficiency Bonus, rounded down.
Make a separate Qiweaving Check for each pattern that is not ended automatically.
###### Certain Unweave
Augment - 1 CP: The automatic-ending threshold becomes your Proficiency Bonus instead of half your Proficiency Bonus.

source_rows.effect:
#### DIRTY TRICK
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: Natural reach
Cost: None
Attempt an underhanded maneuver against one creature you can physically hinder.
Describe the method: throw grit into its eyes, knot a sleeve, stamp on a foot, box its ears, loosen a belt, hook a leg, slap a talisman across its vision, overturn a stool beneath it, or use another plausible tactic.
Make a Scoundrel Check against the target.
Success: Choose one appropriate result:
Eyes Spoiled. The target has the Blinded condition until the start of your next turn.
Ears Ringing. The target has the Deafened condition until the start of your next turn.
Tangled Footwork. Halve the target’s Speed until the start of your next turn.
Low Sweep. The target has the Prone condition.
Jammed Guard. The target cannot take Reactions until the start of your next turn.
Open the Guard. Apply Exploited Opening.
The GM may approve a comparable effect when the description, anatomy, and surroundings support it. A base Dirty Trick should not inflict a stronger condition than those listed above.
A creature without the relevant anatomy or vulnerability is immune to an inappropriate effect.
If a talent extends a physical Dirty Trick beyond the start of your next turn, the target or an adjacent creature can normally take the Utilize action to end that physical hindrance early.

source_rows.effect:
#### STEAL
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: Natural reach
Cost: None
Choose one accessible object. Attempt to take it, reposition it, or plant one Tiny object in an accessible location.
##### Aware Target
Make a Scoundrel Check against the creature.
##### Unaware Target
Make a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check against the target’s Passive Perception.
##### Difficult Object
Make your check with Disadvantage if the object is securely fastened, worn tightly, held in two hands, or similarly difficult to remove.
##### Success
Choose one appropriate result:
take the object into a free hand;
cause the object to fall into an unoccupied space within your reach;
reposition the object to another accessible location on the same target;
plant one Tiny object in an accessible location on the target.
You may use Steal to remove an object from a creature’s hand as a local Scoundrel disarm rule.
Steal does not automatically activate, identify, attune to, or safely handle the object.

#### Carry Voice
Classification: Basic Sound Technique
Action Type: Multi-Mode
Canonical Action Type: Multi-Mode
Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action
Timing Detail: Bonus Action or 1 minute
Factory Routing: bonus_action_plus_extended_message_procedure
Split Review Decision: single_combat_action_plus_procedure_variant
Recommended Factory Realization: procedures=ONE_MINUTE_EXTENDED_VOICE
Range: 120 feet normally, or longer through prepared echoes
Cost: None, or 1 CP for extended use
You can carry a brief message to one creature you can see within 120 feet. The target hears the message as a whisper, tone, bell-note, or inner vibration. This does not require the target to share a language, but the message must be understandable by ordinary means.
By spending 1 CP and concentrating for 1 minute, you may send a short message to a familiar location, prepared bell, resonant object, or creature whose voice you have studied within 1 mile. The target hears the message if a path of sound, structure, spirit resonance, or prepared anchor reasonably exists.
Carry Voice is not telepathy. Barriers, Silence, anti-divination wards, distance, or hostile territory may block it.

#### Dampen Sound
Classification: Basic Sound Technique
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 30 feet
Area: 10-foot cube
Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute
Cost: 1 CP
Create a zone of controlled dampening.
For the duration:
ordinary sound from inside the area is muffled;
creatures outside the area have Disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks relying on hearing to notice sounds from inside;
creatures inside have Advantage on checks to move quietly if the only issue is sound;
Thunder damage dealt entirely inside the area is reduced by your Proficiency Bonus.
Dampen Sound is not full magical Silence. It does not prevent verbal components, speech, command words, or thunder damage unless a talent upgrades it.

#### Read the Vibration
Classification: Basic Sound Technique
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 60 feet
Cost: None
Listen to vibration in air, ground, water, walls, objects, weapons, or living bodies.
Make a Sound Check against a DC set by the GM or opposed by a relevant Dexterity (Stealth), Dexterity (Sleight of Hand), Wisdom (Perception), or cultivation concealment check.
On a success, learn one:
whether a creature moved through a nearby space recently;
whether a wall, door, vessel, bell, bridge, or barrier is hollow, cracked, tensioned, sealed, or reinforced;
whether an invisible or hidden creature is making meaningful sound within range;
whether an object or structure is resonant, brittle, or warded against sound;
whether a spoken phrase, bell, song, or chant carries supernatural influence.
Read the Vibration does not automatically reveal exact location, see through walls, identify all creatures, or bypass stealth. It provides a clue or contested perception method.

#### Resonant Note
Classification: Basic Sound Technique
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 60 feet
Target: One creature or object you can perceive
Cost: None
Make a Sound Cultivation Attack against the target.
Hit: The target takes Thunder damage and gains your Resonance until the start of your next turn.
Damage by Cultivation Level:
CL 1-4: 1d8 Thunder damage.
CL 5-10: 2d8 Thunder damage.
CL 11-16: 3d8 Thunder damage.
CL 17-20: 4d8 Thunder damage.
If the target is an unattended object, brittle structure, ordinary barrier, or construct, add your Proficiency Bonus to the damage.
If the target already bears your Resonance, choose one rider on a hit:
the target is Deafened until the start of your next turn;
the target has Disadvantage on the next Concentration saving throw it makes before the start of your next turn;
the target cannot benefit from ordinary sound-based hiding until the start of your next turn;
if the target is an object or barrier, the next damage it takes before the start of your next turn ignores ordinary Resistance to Thunder damage.

source_rows.effect:
### Base Ability - Fold Step
Tag: Fold Art.
Action Type: Bonus Action
Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: Self.
Cost: 1 CP.
Teleport up to 20 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.
You may bring worn and carried equipment.
Fold Step does not provoke Opportunity Attacks because you do not move through the intervening spaces.
Fold Step cannot pass through Dimensional Lock, a sealed formation, a closed spatial boundary, or a stronger Space effect.
Scaling:
Fold Step does not gain automatic range from CL. Its ordinary range improves through Extended Fold and similar explicit talents. This keeps the base technique reliable while making investment matter.
Ordinary Cap: Unless a higher-Realm talent, anchor, Domain, or variant explicitly says otherwise, ordinary unassisted Fold Step cannot exceed 50 feet. Fifty feet of uninterrupted teleportation with no path drawback is already a powerful battlefield movement tool.
Fold Step is a battlefield step, not long-distance travel magic.

### Base Ability - Spatial Awareness
Tag: Anchor Art.
Action Type: Multi-Mode
Canonical Action Type: Multi-Mode
Factory Combat Bucket: split_required
Split Candidate Buckets: action, passive
Timing Detail: Passive and Action
Factory Routing: split_modes_before_character_action_programming
Split Review Decision: split_required_distinct_combat_buckets
Recommended Factory Realization: modes=PASSIVE_SPATIAL_AWARENESS->passive, ACTION_ACTIVE_INSPECTION->action
Range: 60 feet.
Cost: 0 CP for passive awareness; 1 CP to inspect actively.
Passive Effect: You sense obvious spatial disturbances within range. You know when a creature you can perceive teleports, opens a portal, enters or exits a pocket space, uses extradimensional storage, crosses a planar boundary, or forces a space wider or narrower than it should be.
Active Inspection: As an Action, spend 1 CP and choose one creature, object, doorway, area, or visible spatial effect within range. Make a Cultivation Check against the effect’s creator or against a DC set by rarity and concealment.
On a success, learn up to two of the following:
whether the target is spatially sealed;
whether the target has teleported within the last hour;
whether the target carries extradimensional storage;
whether the target is linked to an anchor;
whether a doorway or surface hides a pocket space;
whether a barrier blocks teleportation;
the approximate CL of the spatial effect;
whether the disturbance is stable, decaying, trapped, or contested.
Spatial Awareness does not reveal secret doors unless they are spatially distorted, and it does not identify ordinary locks.

source_rows.effect:
### Spirit Regard
When you successfully Read the Spirit Nature, you may place a Spirit Regard on the target.
Spirit Regard lasts for 1 hour, until you dismiss it, until the target is no longer on the same plane or layer of reality, or until the target hides its Nature with a stronger effect.
You have Advantage on the next Charisma, Wisdom, or Cultivation Check you make to communicate with, soothe, bargain with, bind, host, exorcise, or command a target bearing your Spirit Regard.
You may maintain a number of Spirit Regards equal to your Proficiency Bonus.

source_rows.effect:
### Temporary Scene Bond
As an Action, you may spend 1 CP to create a temporary bond with a willing minor spirit, a spirit bearing your Spirit Regard, or a spirit whose Need you immediately satisfy.
The bond lasts for 1 scene.
During that scene, you may ask the spirit for one minor service, one piece of advice, one omen, one safe passage, one momentary manifestation, or one simple Nature Expression approved by the GM.
Temporary Scene Bonds do not count against your Major Spirit Bond limit unless the spirit fights for you or uses a major sphere effect.

source_rows.effect:
### Black Trace
**Action Type:** Action
**Range:** 30 feet
**Target:** One creature or object you can see
**Cost:** None
Make a ranged Cultivation Attack.
On hit, the target takes Ruin damage based on your Realm.
| Realm | Safe Black Trace Damage |
|---|---:|
| Mortal | 1d10 + your Unmaking key ability modifier |
| Foundation | 2d10 + your Unmaking key ability modifier |
| Core Formation | 3d10 + your Unmaking key ability modifier |
| Nascent Soul | 4d10 + your Unmaking key ability modifier |
On hit, choose one Trace effect:
**Fray.** The target cannot regain HP until the start of your next turn.
**Crack.** If the target is an object, construct, armor, shield, barrier, or temporary qi structure, it takes additional Ruin damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
**Sting.** The target cannot take Reactions against you until the start of your next turn.
**Mark.** The next Unmaking talent that damages the target before the end of your next turn deals additional Ruin damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
You may Overdraw when Black Trace hits.
#### Unbound Trace
Before making the Black Trace attack, you may make the Trace unstable.
On hit, the damage becomes the Unbound Trace value instead.
| Realm | Unbound Trace Damage |
|---|---:|
| Mortal | 2d10 + your Unmaking key ability modifier |
| Foundation | 4d10 + your Unmaking key ability modifier |
| Core Formation | 6d10 + your Unmaking key ability modifier |
| Nascent Soul | 8d10 + your Unmaking key ability modifier |
After the attack resolves, whether it hits or misses, choose one:
- gain 1 Black Vein Strain;
- take Ruin self-damage equal to **1d6 + your Proficiency Bonus**;
- one suitable focus, needle, talisman, weapon, or External Channel gains 1 Crack.
You may Overdraw when Unbound Trace hits.
---

source_rows.effect:
### Ruin Channel
**Action Type:** Bonus Action
**Range:** Self or touch
**Cost:** None
**Duration:** Until the start of your next turn
You run Unmaking qi through one Channel you are touching.
Choose one:
- a held weapon;
- an unarmed strike;
- one hand or limb;
- a talisman, needle, chain, or tool;
- another object the GM agrees can briefly hold Unmaking qi.
The next time before the duration ends that you hit with that Channel, deal additional Ruin damage based on your Realm.
| Realm | Ruin Channel Bonus Damage |
|---|---:|
| Mortal | 2d8 |
| Foundation | 3d8 |
| Core Formation | 5d8 |
| Nascent Soul | 7d8 |
After the attack resolves, choose one cost:
- the Channel gains 1 Crack if it is an External Channel;
- you gain 1 Black Vein Strain if it is an Internal Channel;
- you take Ruin self-damage equal to **1d6 + your Proficiency Bonus**, and the Channel does not gain Crack or Strain.
If the attack misses, the Channel remains active until the duration ends. If the duration ends without a hit, you take Ruin self-damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
Ruin Channel may be applied to a ranged weapon, thrown weapon, or ammunition only if you are touching it when you use the feature.
You may Overdraw when a Ruin Channel attack hits.

### Feed the Root
Action Type: No Action
Factory Combat Bucket: passive
Factory Routing: passive_or_triggered_modifier_row
Trigger: You place a Growth Mark on a creature, object, or space touching one of your Living Claims
Use Limit: Once per turn
Choose one of your Living Claims within 60 feet.
It gains one Root Feed until the end of your next turn.
A Living Claim can hold Root Feed up to your Proficiency Bonus.
When you use a Verdant Response from or through that Living Claim, you may spend 1 Root Feed as if it were 1 Growth Mark on the affected creature, space, or object.
Root Feed represents the growth itself being fed by pressure, blood, breath, water, motion, or attention.

### Sow Living Claim
Action Type: Bonus Action
Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row

Duration: 1 minute
Cost: 0 CP
Create one Living Claim in a legal Living Medium.

You may have a number of Living Claims active equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
If you create a Living Claim beyond this number, choose one old Living Claim to wither.

Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 60 feet
Target: One creature, object, or temporary Barrier
Cost: None
Make a ranged Cultivation Attack.
Hit: Deal damage of your default Void type.
CL: 1-4;
Damage: 1d8
CL: 5-10;
Damage: 2d8
CL: 11-16;
Damage: 3d8
CL: 17+;
Damage: 4d8
Once per turn when Void Needle hits, choose one Void Pressure.
#### Empty Vitality
The target cannot gain Temporary HP until the start of your next turn.
#### Cost Lock
The target cannot reduce CP, Stamina, or other printed technique costs below the listed cost until the start of your next turn.
#### Unsettle Invisibility
The target cannot gain the Invisible condition from an ordinary temporary supernatural effect until the start of your next turn.
This does not reveal a creature that is already Hidden.
#### Fray Barrier
If the target is a temporary Barrier, reduce its HP by your Proficiency Bonus in addition to the damage dealt.

source_rows.effect:
### Base Sphere Abilities
When you first gain the Sphere of Wax, you gain Mold Wax, Press Seal, and Kindle Wax.
You also learn one Wax talent of your choice.
#### Mold Wax
Action. Range 60 feet. Cost 1 CP. Duration Concentration, up to 1 minute.
You create or awaken cultivated wax in an unoccupied space, on a surface, or over an unattended object within range. Choose one form.
Soft Spread. You create a 10-foot square of Soft Wax on a surface. The area is Difficult Terrain for hostile creatures. The first hostile creature each round that enters the area or starts its turn there must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or become impressed by the wax until the end of your next turn.
Set Shape. You create a Set Wax panel, ramp, handhold, brace, small bridge, shield plate, low wall, or similar structure that fits within two contiguous 5-foot cubes. It must be supported by a surface unless a talent says otherwise. It can provide cover, block a narrow passage, support weight, or create a short ramp or platform.
Fine Work. Outside initiative, you can shape wax into seals, molds, masks, tablets, candle forms, practice tools, ritual counters, labels, evidence casts, and small sculptures. Fine Work cannot create valuable trade goods, magical items, living organs, or permanent infrastructure unless the GM says otherwise.
At CL 5, your Soft Spread can cover a 15-foot square, or your Set Shape can fit within four contiguous 5-foot cubes.
At CL 10, your Soft Spread can cover a 20-foot square, or your Set Shape can fit within six contiguous 5-foot cubes.
At CL 15, your Soft Spread can cover a 25-foot square, or your Set Shape can fit within eight contiguous 5-foot cubes.
#### Press Seal
Action. Range 30 feet. Cost 1 CP. Duration 1 minute.
You press or throw a cultivated Wax Seal onto one creature, object, surface, or 5-foot space within range. A willing creature, unattended object, or surface is sealed automatically. An unwilling creature or attended object makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, the seal attaches. On a success, the seal fails.
When you place the seal, choose one base seal.
Clinging Seal. The sealed creature’s Speed is reduced by 10 feet while the seal remains. If placed on an object, the object adheres to the surface it touches and requires an Action and a successful Strength check against your Cultivation Save DC to remove.
Witness Seal. The seal records the next creature other than you that touches, opens, damages, moves, or passes through the sealed target. You know that the seal was triggered if you are within 1 mile, and you can later inspect the seal to see the outline, handprint, footprint, tool mark, weapon shape, or other physical Impression left behind.
Closing Seal. The seal holds a door, lid, drawer, container, wound wrapping, sheath, scroll case, coffin, or similar closure shut. Opening it requires an Action and a successful Strength check or Dexterity check with appropriate tools against your Cultivation Save DC. A creature can also destroy the seal normally.
Preserving Seal. The sealed object, corpse, medicine, food, blood sample, written page, track, footprint, wound dressing, or physical clue resists decay, contamination, smearing, and ordinary weather while the seal remains.
#### Kindle Wax
Bonus Action. Range 60 feet. Cost 0 CP.
You burn one Wax form, Wax Seal, candle, or wax object you created within range. The chosen wax is consumed. Choose one base release.
Candleflare. One creature within 5 feet of the kindled wax makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, it takes fire damage equal to 1d6 + your Proficiency Bonus. On a success, it takes half damage.
Smoke Puff. The wax releases thick smoke in a 5-foot radius until the start of your next turn. The area is Lightly Obscured. This smoke is ordinary smoke once released and can be dispersed by strong wind.
Release Seal. If the kindled wax was a Wax Seal on an ally, the ally gains temporary hit points equal to your Proficiency Bonus. If it was a Wax Seal on an enemy, that enemy takes fire damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
Mark the Wick. You learn whether the wax had been touched, moved, damaged, or disturbed since you created it. If it held an Impression, you preserve a brief sensory image of the Impression before the wax burns.

#### Press Seal
Action. Range 30 feet. Cost 1 CP. Duration 1 minute.
You press or throw a cultivated Wax Seal onto one creature, object, surface, or 5-foot space within range. A willing creature, unattended object, or surface is sealed automatically. An unwilling creature or attended object makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, the seal attaches. On a success, the seal fails.
When you place the seal, choose one base seal.
Clinging Seal. The sealed creature’s Speed is reduced by 10 feet while the seal remains. If placed on an object, the object adheres to the surface it touches and requires an Action and a successful Strength check against your Cultivation Save DC to remove.
Witness Seal. The seal records the next creature other than you that touches, opens, damages, moves, or passes through the sealed target. You know that the seal was triggered if you are within 1 mile, and you can later inspect the seal to see the outline, handprint, footprint, tool mark, weapon shape, or other physical Impression left behind.
Closing Seal. The seal holds a door, lid, drawer, container, wound wrapping, sheath, scroll case, coffin, or similar closure shut. Opening it requires an Action and a successful Strength check or Dexterity check with appropriate tools against your Cultivation Save DC. A creature can also destroy the seal normally.
Preserving Seal. The sealed object, corpse, medicine, food, blood sample, written page, track, footprint, wound dressing, or physical clue resists decay, contamination, smearing, and ordinary weather while the seal remains.

#### Applying a Rising Mark
You can apply a Rising Mark in three basic ways.
Kindle the Rising. As a Bonus Action, choose yourself or one willing creature, unattended object, or ongoing effect you created within 60 feet that you can perceive. The target gains one Kindled Mark.
Force the Rising. As a Reaction when a creature, object, or effect within 60 feet that you can perceive hits with an attack, forces a saving throw, regains Hit Points, gains Temporary HP, spends CP, uses a spell slot, uses a limited feature, teleports, becomes Hidden, becomes Invisible, creates concealment, creates an illusion, or moves at least 10 feet during its turn, you may apply one Overkindled Mark to the source after the triggering event resolves.
Rising Thread. As an Action, make a ranged Cultivation Attack against one creature or object within 60 feet. On a hit, the target takes Fire, Radiant, or Force damage, chosen when you make the attack, and gains one Overkindled Mark.
| Cultivation Level | Rising Thread Damage |
| --- | --- |
| CL 1-4 | 1d6 |
| CL 5-10 | 2d6 |
| CL 11-16 | 3d6 |
| CL 17-20 | 4d6 |
The damage is not the sphere’s identity. It is the visible symptom of qi becoming too bright, too hot, or too forceful to remain unfinished.

source_rows.effect:
### BASE SPHERE ABILITIES
The Yang sphere uses Rising Marks. A Rising Mark is not a condition. Immunity to a condition does not grant immunity to Rising Marks unless a feature says otherwise.
A Rising Mark represents a motion, wound, breath, oath, technique, or intention that has begun to swell toward completion.
#### Mark Limit
You can maintain a number of Rising Marks equal to your Proficiency Bonus. A creature, object, or ongoing effect can have only one Rising Mark from you at a time unless a feature says otherwise.
A Rising Mark lasts until the end of your next turn, until you spend it, or until the marked subject is no longer on the same plane of existence as you.
#### Kindled and Overkindled Marks
A Rising Mark has one of two expressions.
Kindled Mark. A Rising Mark on you, a willing creature, an unattended object, or an effect you created is a Kindled Mark. You spend Kindled Marks to help an action complete.
Overkindled Mark. A Rising Mark on an unwilling creature, hostile object, enemy effect, or creature that rejects your assistance is an Overkindled Mark. You spend Overkindled Marks to make hostile exertion overcomplete, exposing or straining the source.
A willing creature may end your Rising Mark on itself at any time, no Action required.
#### Applying a Rising Mark
You can apply a Rising Mark in three basic ways.
Kindle the Rising. As a Bonus Action, choose yourself or one willing creature, unattended object, or ongoing effect you created within 60 feet that you can perceive. The target gains one Kindled Mark.
Force the Rising. As a Reaction when a creature, object, or effect within 60 feet that you can perceive hits with an attack, forces a saving throw, regains Hit Points, gains Temporary HP, spends CP, uses a spell slot, uses a limited feature, teleports, becomes Hidden, becomes Invisible, creates concealment, creates an illusion, or moves at least 10 feet during its turn, you may apply one Overkindled Mark to the source after the triggering event resolves.
Rising Thread. As an Action, make a ranged Cultivation Attack against one creature or object within 60 feet. On a hit, the target takes Fire, Radiant, or Force damage, chosen when you make the attack, and gains one Overkindled Mark.
| Cultivation Level | Rising Thread Damage |
| --- | --- |
| CL 1-4 | 1d6 |
| CL 5-10 | 2d6 |
| CL 11-16 | 3d6 |
| CL 17-20 | 4d6 |
The damage is not the sphere’s identity. It is the visible symptom of qi becoming too bright, too hot, or too forceful to remain unfinished.
#### Spending a Rising Mark
Once per round, when a marked subject you can perceive performs a triggering act, you may spend its Rising Mark without using an Action. Choose one Completing Response appropriate to the mark.
#### Kindled Responses
You may use these responses when you spend a Kindled Mark.
Complete Force.
Trigger: the marked subject deals damage. Add 1d6 + your Key Ability modifier to one damage roll. This bonus increases to 2d6 at CL 5, 3d6 at CL 11, and 4d6 at CL 17.
Complete Aim.
Trigger: the marked subject makes an attack roll or forces one or more creatures to make a saving throw. Add 1d4 to the attack roll, or choose one target making the saving throw and subtract 1d4 from that saving throw. At CL 11, the die becomes 1d6.
Complete Step.
Trigger: the marked subject begins movement during its turn. Increase one of the subject’s Speeds by 10 feet until the end of the current turn, or allow it to stand from Prone without spending movement. At CL 11, the Speed increase becomes 20 feet.
Complete Breath.
Trigger: the marked subject regains Hit Points or gains Temporary HP. Increase the amount gained by your Proficiency Bonus + your Key Ability modifier.
Complete Resolve.
Trigger: the marked subject makes a saving throw against an effect that would reduce its Speed, prevent it from taking Reactions, impose Frightened, Paralyzed, Restrained, Stunned, or Unconscious, or suppress its ability to act. Add 1d4 to the saving throw. At CL 11, the die becomes 1d6.
Complete Revelation.
Trigger: the marked subject makes an attack roll, Wisdom (Perception) check, or Intelligence (Investigation) check against a creature or effect that is Hidden, Invisible, heavily obscured, disguised by illusion, or concealed by a Yin-like technique. The marked subject ignores Disadvantage from not seeing the target for that roll, provided it can still identify the target’s space or general location.
#### Overkindled Responses
You may use these responses when you spend an Overkindled Mark.
Overheat Force.
Trigger: the marked subject deals damage, makes an attack roll, or forces one or more creatures to make a saving throw. After the triggering act resolves, the subject takes Fire or Radiant damage equal to 1d6 + your Key Ability modifier. This damage increases to 2d6 at CL 5, 3d6 at CL 11, and 4d6 at CL 17.
Overexpose.
Trigger: the marked subject becomes Hidden, becomes Invisible, creates concealment, creates an illusion, or benefits from a feature that prevents others from perceiving it. Until the start of your next turn, the subject cannot benefit from being Hidden or Invisible against you, and allies you choose within 60 feet know the subject’s current space if they can perceive the area.
Overcommit Step.
Trigger: the marked subject moves at least 10 feet, teleports, or uses special movement. After the movement resolves, the subject cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn. If the movement was teleportation and the destination is within 120 feet of you, you know the destination space.
Overgrown Recovery.
Trigger: the marked subject regains Hit Points, gains Temporary HP, restores CP, or benefits from regeneration. Until the start of your next turn, the first damage roll against that subject gains a bonus equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
Overstrain Technique.
Trigger: the marked subject spends CP, uses a spell slot, activates a limited feature, or uses a named cultivation technique. If the subject uses the same named spell, sphere talent, forged technique, monster action, or cultivation ability again before the end of its next turn, it gains a Rising Mark immediately after the repeated ability resolves.
#### Yang Saves
Some Yang features require a saving throw. Unless a feature says otherwise, your Cultivation Save DC equals your Cultivation Save DC.

Trigger: the marked subject makes an attack roll or forces one or more creatures to make a saving throw. Add 1d4 to the attack roll, or choose one target making the saving throw and subtract 1d4 from that saving throw. At CL 11, the die becomes 1d6.
Complete Step.
Trigger: the marked subject begins movement during its turn. Increase one of the subject’s Speeds by 10 feet until the end of the current turn, or allow it to stand from Prone without spending movement. At CL 11, the Speed increase becomes 20 feet.
Complete Breath.
Trigger: the marked subject regains Hit Points or gains Temporary HP. Increase the amount gained by your Proficiency Bonus + your Key Ability modifier.
Complete Resolve.
Trigger: the marked subject makes a saving throw against an effect that would reduce its Speed, prevent it from taking Reactions, impose Frightened, Paralyzed, Restrained, Stunned, or Unconscious, or suppress its ability to act. Add 1d4 to the saving throw. At CL 11, the die becomes 1d6.
Complete Revelation.
Trigger: the marked subject makes an attack roll, Wisdom (Perception) check, or Intelligence (Investigation) check against a creature or effect that is Hidden, Invisible, heavily obscured, disguised by illusion, or concealed by a Yin-like technique. Overexpose.
Trigger: the marked subject becomes Hidden, becomes Invisible, creates concealment, creates an illusion, or benefits from a feature that prevents others from perceiving it. Trigger: the marked subject moves at least 10 feet, teleports, or uses special movement. After the movement resolves, the subject cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn. If the movement was teleportation and the destination is within 120 feet of you, you know the destination space.
Overgrown Recovery.
Trigger: the marked subject regains Hit Points, gains Temporary HP, restores CP, or benefits from regeneration. Until the start of your next turn, the first damage roll against that subject gains a bonus equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
Overstrain Technique.
Trigger: the marked subject spends CP, uses a spell slot, activates a limited feature, or uses a named cultivation technique. ### BASE SPHERE ABILITIES
The Yang sphere uses Rising Marks. A Rising Mark is not a condition. Immunity to a condition does not grant immunity to Rising Marks unless a feature says otherwise.
A Rising Mark represents a motion, wound, breath, oath, technique, or intention that has begun to swell toward completion.
#### Mark Limit
You can maintain a number of Rising Marks equal to your Proficiency Bonus. A creature, object, or ongoing effect can have only one Rising Mark from you at a time unless a feature says otherwise.
A Rising Mark lasts until the end of your next turn, until you spend it, or until the marked subject is no longer on the same plane of existence as you.
#### Kindled and Overkindled Marks
A Rising Mark has one of two expressions.
Kindled Mark. A Rising Mark on you, a willing creature, an unattended object, or an effect you created is a Kindled Mark. You spend Kindled Marks to help an action complete.
Overkindled Mark. A Rising Mark on an unwilling creature, hostile object, enemy effect, or creature that rejects your assistance is an Overkindled Mark. You spend Overkindled Marks to make hostile exertion overcomplete, exposing or straining the source.
A willing creature may end your Rising Mark on itself at any time, no Action required.
#### Applying a Rising Mark
You can apply a Rising Mark in three basic ways.
Kindle the Rising. As a Bonus Action, choose yourself or one willing creature, unattended object, or ongoing effect you created within 60 feet that you can perceive. The target gains one Kindled Mark.
Force the Rising. | CL 1-4 | 1d6 |
| CL 5-10 | 2d6 |
| CL 11-16 | 3d6 |

source_rows.effect:
### BASE SPHERE ABILITIES
The Yin sphere uses Waning Marks. A Waning Mark is not a condition. Immunity to a condition does not grant immunity to Waning Marks unless a feature says otherwise.
A Waning Mark represents a motion, technique, wound, breath, or intention that has begun to decline before it finishes expressing itself.
#### Mark Limit
You can maintain a number of Waning Marks equal to your Proficiency Bonus. A creature can have only one Waning Mark from you at a time unless a feature says otherwise.
A Waning Mark lasts until the end of your next turn, until you spend it, or until the marked creature is no longer on the same plane of existence as you.
#### Marking a Creature
You can apply a Waning Mark in three basic ways.
Mark the Waning. As a Bonus Action, choose one creature within 60 feet that you can see, hear, or otherwise perceive clearly. The target gains one Waning Mark.
Receive Overextension. As a Reaction when a creature within 60 feet that you can perceive hits with an attack, forces a saving throw, regains Hit Points, gains Temporary HP, spends CP, uses a spell slot, teleports, or moves at least 10 feet during its turn, you may apply one Waning Mark to that creature after the triggering event resolves.
Withdrawing Thread. As an Action, make a ranged Cultivation Attack against one creature or object within 60 feet. On a hit, the target takes Cold or Necrotic damage, chosen when you make the attack, and gains one Waning Mark.
| Cultivation Level | Withdrawing Thread Damage |
| --- | --- |
| CL 1-4 | 1d6 |
| CL 5-10 | 2d6 |
| CL 11-16 | 3d6 |
| CL 17-20 | 4d6 |
The damage is not the sphere’s identity. It is the visible symptom of qi cooling as the target’s action begins to wane.
#### Spending a Waning Mark
Once per round, when a marked creature you can perceive performs a triggering act, you may spend its Waning Mark without using an Action. Choose one Diminishing Response appropriate to the trigger.
**Diminish Force**
Trigger: the marked creature deals damage. Reduce one damage roll by 1d6 + your Key Ability modifier. This reduction increases to 2d6 at CL 5, 3d6 at CL 11, and 4d6 at CL 17.
**Diminish Aim**
Trigger: the marked creature makes an attack roll. Subtract 1d4 from the attack roll. At CL 11, subtract 1d6 instead.
**Diminish Power**
Trigger: the marked creature forces one or more creatures to make a saving throw. Choose one creature making that saving throw. The chosen creature adds 1d4 to the saving throw. At CL 11, the bonus becomes 1d6.
**Diminish Step**
Trigger: the marked creature begins movement, including teleportation. Reduce one of the creature’s Speeds by 10 feet until the end of the current turn, or reduce the distance of one teleportation effect by 10 feet. At CL 11, the reduction becomes 20 feet.
**Diminish Recovery**
Trigger: the marked creature regains Hit Points, gains Temporary HP, restores CP, or benefits from regeneration. Reduce the amount gained or restored by your Proficiency Bonus + your Key Ability modifier, to a minimum of 0.
**Diminish Readiness**
Trigger: the marked creature takes a Reaction or would gain Advantage on a roll. The creature cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn, or the triggering Advantage is canceled for that roll.
#### Yin Saves
Some Yin features require a saving throw. Unless a feature says otherwise, your Cultivation Save DC equals your Cultivation Save DC.
#### Marked Allies
You may place a Waning Mark on a willing ally. When you do, the mark represents preservation rather than harm. You may spend that mark only for Diminish Force, Diminish Power, Diminish Step, or Diminish Recovery if doing so benefits the ally.
A willing creature may end your Waning Mark on itself at any time, no Action required.
